title: GuardianPlug: A Portable, Self-Learning, Pole–Zero-Guided Electrical Safety System for Unknown Worksites
content: Electricity can seriously hurt a person if it flows through their body, and this can happen in less than a second. Ordinary safety switches help, but they are set to one fixed level and can take up to a fraction of a second to cut the power. This paper describes GuardianPlug, a small, portable safety device that plugs into any wall socket. It works in two easy steps. First it learns the electrical circuit it is plugged into, the way a new guard learns a building on the first day. Then it watches all the time, and the moment it senses that electricity might be passing through a person, it switches the power off extremely fast—in about 15 millionths of a second (15 µs), far quicker than normal switches. GuardianPlug also has a special sentinel mode for wires that are meant to be switched off. If a worker is fixing a “dead” circuit and the power suddenly comes back on by mistake, the device notices the sudden electricity at once, cuts it off, and sounds an alarm. Because it learns each new place, GuardianPlug can be used on building sites, in workshops, or anywhere the wiring is unknown: a worker simply plugs it in, waits for the green Safe light, and starts work. This paper explains the idea, shows how the device could be built (with diagrams), and lists the safety rules it should meet. The design is a proposal; real versions would still need careful laboratory testing before they can be trusted to protect people.
